what_happened: The record's own absorbing duplicate (completed/archived task 373, null_resolution_entries_unreachable_by_conclusion_stage) was found live in this repository's specs/archive/ tree, confirming the dispatch's DISPOSITION PENDING note was correct: the resolution-field half of the defect is fixed, verified byte-identical between agent-system/extensions/core/context/{contracts/conclusion-stage.md,formats/issue-log.md} and the deployed .claude/ mirror, with implicit_open_count present in both the contract and the live orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh --aggregate output.

The dispatch's DISPOSITION PENDING block treated the 'where does a transplant go when the absorbing record is already closed' question as unresolved, pointing at a foreign repository's record 481 that does not resolve here. A repository-local governing document, agent-system/extensions/core/context/patterns/cross-repo-task-migration.md's 'Duplicates: transplant before abandoning' section, already states the general rule directly: if amending the absorbing record is not possible, do not abandon the duplicate -- report it and leave it open. No foreign record needs to resolve; this repository's own migration-pattern document already answers the fail-safe case task 562 is in.

Independent reproduction of transplant item (i) did not require cross-repo access to a foreign fixture: a live, currently-active task in this repository (436_orient_command_with_scout_agent_retire_review) already carries 9 null-resolution, null-suggested_channel, kind:issue entries spanning minor and costly severity. Running orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh --aggregate (read-only) against it reproduced the post-fix behavior exactly: all 9 reached classification as 7 proposals (one class grouping 3 entries), implicit_open_count=9, 3 kind:win entries correctly exempted, and every proposal's suggested_channel_hints was an empty array -- corroborating both the reproduction-at-higher-severity requirement and the proposal-volume datum from a second, independent run.
